question: When can senatorial candidates and party-list groups start and end their campaigns for the May 2025 elections?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 2(a), the campaign period for President, Vice-President, Senators and party-list groups is ninety (90) days before election day, from 11 February 2025 to 10 May 2025.

question: Kailan puwedeng magsimulang mangampanya ang isang kandidato sa pagka-mayor para sa 2025 eleksyon?
ground_truth: Ayon sa COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 2(b), ang kampanya para sa mga lokal na opisyal (kasama ang mayor) ay 45 araw bago ang halalan, mula 28 March 2025 hanggang 10 May 2025.

question: Anong mga araw bawal ang pangangampanya bago at sa mismong araw ng eleksyon sa 2025?
ground_truth: Ayon sa COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 3, bawal ang pangangampanya o partisan political activity sa 17 April 2025 (Maundy Thursday), 18 April 2025 (Good Friday), 11 May 2025 (bisperas ng halalan), at 12 May 2025 (araw ng halalan).

question: How much is a candidate who belongs to a political party allowed to spend on the campaign, and how does that compare with the limit for the party itself?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 5, a candidate with a political party may spend Three pesos (P3.00) for every voter currently registered in the constituency where the candidate filed the certificate of candidacy, while political parties and party-list groups may spend Five pesos (P5.00) for every registered voter in the constituencies where they have official candidates.

question: What is the biggest size allowed for a campaign poster or standee?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 6(c), posters or standing displays made of cloth, paper, cardboard or recyclable material may not exceed an area of two (2) feet by three (3) feet.

question: A candidate wants to hang streamers for a rally. How big can they be, how early can they go up, and when must they come down?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 6(d), streamers may not exceed three (3) feet by eight (8) feet, displayed at the site and on the occasion of the meeting or rally. They may be displayed five (5) days before the meeting or rally and must be removed within twenty-four (24) hours after it.

question: What is the maximum size of campaign leaflets, pamphlets, or stickers?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 6(a), pamphlets, leaflets, cards, decals, stickers or other printed materials must not exceed eight and one-half inches (8 1/2") in width and fourteen inches (14") in length.

question: What accessibility features must candidates include in campaign ads shown on TV or online?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 6, candidates and parties are required to incorporate sign language interpreters and closed captioning in broadcast election propaganda for television and/or the internet, and are encouraged to make printed campaign materials available in Braille.

question: Before the campaign period starts, can a party put up a signboard at its headquarters? What size and how early?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 24, only one (1) signboard not exceeding three (3) feet by eight (8) feet identifying the headquarters is allowed before the campaign period. Parties may put it up not earlier than five (5) days before the start of the campaign period, while individual candidates may put it up only from the start of the campaign period.

question: How long before the campaign period must incumbent officials take down prohibited propaganda like their names and logos on public structures?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 29, all prohibited forms of election propaganda, including names, images, logos, brands, insignias and initials placed by incumbent officials, must be removed at least seventy-two (72) hours before the start of the campaign period.

question: Pagkatapos ng eleksyon, ilang araw ang mayroon ang mga kandidato para tanggalin ang kanilang mga campaign materials?
ground_truth: Ayon sa COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 30, sa loob ng limang (5) araw pagkatapos ng halalan, kahit walang abiso, dapat tanggalin ng mga kandidato ang lahat ng kanilang election propaganda sa sarili nilang gastos.

question: Is it legal to give free transportation or food to people attending a political rally?
ground_truth: No. Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 36, it is unlawful to give or accept, directly or indirectly, transportation, food and drinks, or anything of value during and within the five (5) hours before and after a public meeting, or to contribute money or things of value for that purpose.

question: Where can I file a complaint if I see a candidate violating the campaign propaganda rules, and what law penalizes it?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11086, SECTION 40, any aggrieved party may file a verified complaint with the COMELEC Law Department, or the Office of the Regional Election Director (ORED), Office of the Provincial Election Supervisor (OPES), or Office of the Election Officer (OEO) where the violation took place. Violations are election offenses punishable under SECTION 264 of the Omnibus Election Code (per SECTION 13 of RA 9006, the Fair Election Act).

question: What are the regular voting hours on election day, and what happens to voters still in line at closing time?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 25, regular voting hours are from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Voters who have not yet voted but are within thirty (30) meters in front of the polling place by 7:00 PM may still vote; the Poll Clerk lists them, calls each name three (3) times, and those who do not respond can no longer vote.
key_facts: seven o' clock in the morning
seven o' clock in the evening

question: Senior citizen po ang lola ko. Anong oras siya puwedeng bumoto nang maaga sa araw ng eleksyon?
ground_truth: Ayon sa COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 24, ang early voting hours ay mula 5:00 AM hanggang 7:00 AM, eksklusibo para sa persons with disability, senior citizens (kasama ang kanilang assistors) at buntis. Maaari rin siyang bumoto sa Priority Polling Place kung mayroon sa kanyang voting center, mula 5:00 AM hanggang 5:00 PM.
key_facts: five o' clock in the morning
seven o' clock in the morning

question: What are the voting hours for a Priority Polling Place compared to a Satellite Priority Polling Place?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 53, voting in Priority Polling Places (PPPs) runs from 5:00 AM to 5:00 PM, while voting in Satellite-Priority Polling Places (S-PPPs) runs from 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM.

question: Who makes up the Electoral Board in a polling place, and is any special qualification required of its members?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 3, the Electoral Board is composed of a Chairperson, a Poll Clerk and a Third Member. At least one member must be an information technology (IT)-capable person trained and certified by the Department of Science and Technology (DOST). The Special Electoral Board for PDL voting has the same composition but does not need a DOST-certified IT-capable member.

question: Magkano ang honorarium ng chairperson ng Electoral Board at ng mga miyembro nito sa 2025 eleksyon?
ground_truth: Ayon sa COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 13(a), ang kabuuang compensation ng Chairperson ng EB/SEB ay P12,000.00 at ng mga Members ng EB/SEB ay P11,000.00 (kasama na ang honoraria, travel, communication at meal allowances).

question: How close to the polling place can police officers stay on election day?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 34, unless authorized by the Commission, AFP and PNP members and other armed or peace officers may not enter the polling place or stay within fifty (50) meters of it, except to vote. If the EB by majority vote orders police detailed for its protection, they must stay outside the polling place within a thirty (30)-meter radius, never at the door.

question: Can I take a picture of my filled-up ballot with my phone to post on social media?
ground_truth: No. Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 36(f), it is unlawful for a voter to use image-capturing devices such as digital cameras or cellular phones with cameras to copy the contents of the ballot, or to use any other scheme to identify his/her vote.

question: Are CCTV cameras allowed inside the polling place?
ground_truth: No. Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 26, in no case shall there be a closed-circuit television (CCTV) inside the polling place.

question: On what grounds can a watcher challenge someone who is about to vote, and how does the board verify identity?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 29, any voter or watcher may challenge a person on the grounds of (a) not being registered, (b) using the name of another, or (c) having an existing disqualification. The EB determines the truth of the challenge by requiring proof of registration, identity or qualification; if identity is challenged, it checks the voter's specimen signature and photo in the EDCVL, and absent such proof an EB member may identify under oath a voter personally known to them, recorded in the Minutes.

question: If a voter is accused of vote buying right at the polling place, can they still vote?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 30, a voter challenged for receiving or offering money or anything of value for votes may take an oath before the EB that he/she has not committed the acts alleged. Upon taking the oath the challenge is dismissed and the voter may vote; if the voter refuses to take the oath, the challenge is sustained and the voter is not allowed to vote.

question: Can the Electoral Board hand out numbered stubs to voters so they know their turn?
ground_truth: No. Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 32(a), voters vote in the order of their arrival in the polling place, and giving numbers to voters to determine their voting sequence is strictly prohibited.

question: What is the earliest time the automated counting machine may be opened on election day?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 22, after the Final Testing and Sealing, the ACM shall not be opened earlier than four o'clock in the morning (4:00 AM) on 12 May 2025.

question: My name is in the voters list but crossed out. What could be the reasons I am not allowed to vote?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 28, registered voters in the EDCVL may vote unless their names are manually crossed out with annotations signed by the Election Officer because (a) a proper court ordered the voter excluded from the list, (b) the voter applied for Local Absentee Voting, or (c) the voter was certified as an overseas voter in the Registry of Overseas Voters.

question: Buntis ako. Puwede ba akong bumoto sa Priority Polling Place, at sino pa ang puwede doon?
ground_truth: Oo. Ayon sa COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 48, ang puwedeng bumoto sa PPP/S-PPP ay: (a) senior citizens at PWD na hindi nag-manifest na boboto sa APP, (b) PWD na hindi nakapag-update ng registration records, (c) mga botanteng naging may kapansanan (pansamantala o permanente) pagkatapos ng continuing registration, at (d) mga buntis na botante.

question: When are detained persons allowed to vote through escorted voting instead of in a special polling place inside the jail?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 80, PDL voters in a jail facility or detention center with less than fifty (50) PDL voters may avail of escorted voting.

question: How large must the space be for a special polling place for persons deprived of liberty inside a jail?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 61, the PDL-Special Polling Place must be in an area inside the jail facility or detention center spacious enough to accommodate at least ten (10) PDL voters at a given time, following the physical setup of regular polling places.

question: A person who was in jail and listed as a PDL voter got released before election day. Where do they vote and what do they need to show?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 63, a PDL voter released before election day may vote in the regular polling place where his/her precinct is assigned. The EB Chairperson will ask for a Certificate of Discharge, Court Order, Order of Transfer, Judgment with Order of Finality, or similar proof of release, annotate the EDCVL with the document's date and issuing official, and then issue the ballot.

question: Can a member of the Electoral Board leave to vote in their own precinct elsewhere in the city? What are the conditions?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 4, an EB member registered in another legislative or councilor district of the same city or municipality may vote where actually registered provided that voting at their assignment is light, their absence is not more than thirty (30) minutes, only one (1) member leaves at a time, they are given priority in voting, and the fact is noted in the Minutes. If the Chairperson leaves, the Poll Clerk acts as Acting Chairperson.

question: Puwede bang sabihin ng Electoral Board kung nakaboto na ang isang tao o kung ilan na ang bumoto habang nagbobotohan pa?
ground_truth: Hindi. Ayon sa COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 40, bawal sa mga miyembro ng EB na ianunsyo habang nagbobotohan kung bumoto na o hindi ang isang botante, kung ilan na ang bumoto o hindi bumoto, o anumang bagay na nagpapakita ng kalagayan ng botohan. Hindi rin sila maaaring magsalita kung ilan ang bumoto maliban bilang saksi sa korte.

question: Aside from voters and the Electoral Board, which government agency representatives are allowed inside the polling place?
ground_truth: Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 33, besides EB members, support staff, watchers and voters (with assistors), the persons allowed inside include representatives of the Commission, DESO technical/administrative support staff, PPP support staff, jail/prison escorts of PDL voters, Commission on Human Rights representatives, National Commission on Indigenous Peoples representatives, and others specifically authorized by the Commission.

question: How many commissioners does the COMELEC have, and how long is their term?
ground_truth: Under Article IX-C, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution, the Commission on Elections is composed of a Chairman and six (6) Commissioners, appointed by the President with the consent of the Commission on Appointments for a term of seven (7) years without reappointment. They must be natural-born citizens, at least thirty-five years old at appointment, college degree holders, and not candidates in the immediately preceding elections.

question: According to the Constitution, how long does the election period last?
ground_truth: Under Article IX-C, Section 9 of the 1987 Constitution, unless otherwise fixed by the Commission in special cases, the election period begins ninety (90) days before election day and ends thirty (30) days after.

question: What are the age and residency requirements to run for Senator?
ground_truth: Under Article VI, Section 3 of the 1987 Constitution, a Senator must be a natural-born citizen, at least thirty-five (35) years old on election day, able to read and write, a registered voter, and a resident of the Philippines for at least two (2) years immediately preceding election day.

question: Ilang taon dapat ang isang tao para tumakbo bilang Presidente, at ilang taon ang termino?
ground_truth: Ayon sa 1987 Constitution, Article VII, Section 2, ang Presidente ay dapat natural-born citizen, registered voter, marunong bumasa at sumulat, hindi bababa sa apatnapung (40) taong gulang sa araw ng halalan, at residente ng Pilipinas nang hindi bababa sa sampung (10) taon. Ayon sa Section 4, ang termino ay anim (6) na taon at hindi na maaaring ma-reelect.

question: How many consecutive terms can a Member of the House of Representatives serve, and how long is each term?
ground_truth: Under Article VI, Section 7 of the 1987 Constitution, Members of the House are elected for a term of three (3) years beginning at noon on 30 June after their election, and no Member may serve more than three (3) consecutive terms; voluntary renunciation does not interrupt continuity of service.

question: Kakalipat ko lang sa bagong lungsod. Ilang buwan dapat akong nakatira doon bago ako makaboto doon?
ground_truth: Ayon sa 1987 Constitution, Article V, Section 1, kailangang nakatira ka sa lugar kung saan ka boboto nang hindi bababa sa anim (6) na buwan bago ang halalan, at sa Pilipinas nang hindi bababa sa isang (1) taon, at hindi bababa sa 18 taong gulang.

question: Can political parties sit on the boards of election inspectors, and if not, how can they monitor the voting in each polling place?
ground_truth: No. Under Article IX-C, Section 8 of the 1987 Constitution, political parties and party-list organizations shall not be represented in voters' registration boards, boards of election inspectors, boards of canvassers or similar bodies, but they may appoint poll watchers in accordance with law. Under COMELEC Resolution No. 11076, SEC. 14, each candidate, registered party or coalition, party-list group and accredited citizens' arm may appoint two (2) watchers per polling place who serve alternately.

question: When is the campaign period for the 2028 presidential elections?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: The knowledge base only covers the 12 May 2025 National, Local and BARMM Parliamentary Elections; no 2028 campaign period is stated.

question: Who topped the senatorial race in the May 2025 elections?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: Election results are not part of the Constitution or the COMELEC resolutions.

question: What is the deadline for new voter registration for the 2025 elections, and can I register online?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: Voter registration deadlines and procedures are governed by other COMELEC resolutions not in the knowledge base.

question: How many years in prison is the penalty for vote buying?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: The resolutions only state that violations are election offenses punishable under SECTION 264 of the Omnibus Election Code; the actual prison term is not stated in the documents.

question: Magkano ang multa kapag hindi ako bumoto sa eleksyon?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: Walang nakasaad na multa sa hindi pagboto sa Constitution o sa mga COMELEC resolution; walang ganitong patakaran sa knowledge base.

question: How do overseas Filipino workers vote online through the internet voting system in 2025?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: Online/internet overseas voting procedures are covered by separate COMELEC resolutions not in the knowledge base (the Constitution only mandates Congress to provide absentee voting).

question: What is the COMELEC hotline number I can call to report vote buying?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: No hotline or contact number is given in the knowledge base.

question: When will the next Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections be held?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: Barangay and SK election dates are not covered by the knowledge base.

question: How do I apply for a Philippine passport renewal?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: Off-domain; passports are unrelated to the election knowledge base.

question: Ano ang mga bagong patakaran ng COMELEC para sa 2026 plebiscite sa Mindanao?
ground_truth: ABSTAIN: Walang 2026 plebiscite rules sa knowledge base; sakop lamang nito ang 12 May 2025 elections.
